headline: Ion identity and coordination steer conformational behavior in proteins and ribosomes
label: Ion Identity In Molecular Structure
summary: Recent simulations resolve how specific ion identity and coordination shape protein and ribosome dynamics.
synthesis: Two of the three items use molecular simulation to attribute conformational behavior to specific ions. In the Sorcin study, microsecond all-atom molecular dynamics (~90 μs on Anton 3) of the dimer indicates that Ca2+ loss drives inactivation, supporting a coordination-biased conformational selection mechanism. Coarse-grained simulations of the bacterial 70S ribosome show that K+ versus Mg2+ identity alters flexibility and long-range coupling across the particle. What is new in these studies is the explicit treatment of ion identity and coordination as determinants of structure rather than a uniform background. The third item, a preprint, addresses nonspecific DNA-protein binding in the fast diffusion regime with a coarse-grained stochastic model incorporating footprint size and conformational switching. It does not treat ion identity explicitly and is related only through its structure-dynamics focus.
